01.title: Lilith Asks Who Is Speaking
01.want: Hear the creation account without being folded into Mother's identity
01.obstacle: A foundational narrator's address can make the listener appear to have existed in the narrated scene
01.choice: Ask for the boundary between the remembered creation and their present encounter
01.consequence: Lilith becomes an active recipient who preserves her own standing while creation remains temporally earlier
source_passages: ILLUMINATED_CODEX_COMPLETE.md:916-922, Mother holds and Lilith protects
01.lore_reveal: Framing presence is not physical participation before embodied creation; source/aspect identity remains unresolved
01.humour_target: An ancient storyteller being interrupted for an exceptionally relevant clarification

02.title: The Shelter Lilith Builds
02.want: Make an independent life after refusal without becoming a new household sovereign
02.obstacle: Shelter is scarce and other displaced beings offer obedience in exchange for safety
02.choice: Build a refuge whose occupants keep the ability to leave and contest its rules
02.consequence: Lilith gains neighbours and material obligations beyond Adam's household; her refusal becomes a durable alternative
source_passages: Alphabet of Ben Sira: later Lilith refusal tradition
EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: off-Garden refuge, not scriptural episode
02.lore_reveal: Protection differs from ownership; continuing identity across later clocks requires root world reconciliation
02.humour_target: A determined solitary discovering that an open refuge inevitably needs a roof repaired

03.title: The People the Ark Did Not Name
03.want: Move threatened refuge households beyond the coming water
03.obstacle: Trusted routes fail and patrons offer rescue only to pledged followers
03.choice: Guide an independent evacuation and abandon a refuge she cannot preserve safely
03.consequence: A scattered community survives owing Lilith no perpetual allegiance; the first refuge is irretrievably lost
source_passages: EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: Lilith evacuation, no ancient attestation claimed
03.lore_reveal: Her protective role entails loss; she does not secretly replace Noah or all flood saviours
03.humour_target: Patrons attempting to attach an exclusivity agreement to a boat

04.title: A Promise for the Unchosen
04.want: Keep a route open for households excluded from dynastic protection
04.obstacle: A patron offers reliable provision only if the refuge recognizes one lineage's superior claim
04.choice: Refuse the exclusive patronage and establish reciprocal support between otherwise rival households
04.consequence: A fragile aid route survives outside the covenant households and later offers an alternative to state dependence
source_passages: Genesis 16 and 21 as Hagar comparison, not identity equation
04.lore_reveal: A promise to one household need not imply absence of relation with everyone else
04.humour_target: A sponsorship proposal assuming that universal compassion would benefit from a preferred customer tier

05.title: The Stranger at Lilith's Fire
05.want: Shelter displaced people whose identities the liberation movement distrusts
05.obstacle: Refugees bring injuries and loyalties from both sides of the recent catastrophe
05.choice: Set enforceable rules against coercion while judging each arrival by conduct rather than origin
05.consequence: A mixed refuge preserves lives and testimony outside the victorious community's membership system
source_passages: Exodus 12:38; Exodus 22:20 (NABRE; 22:21 in other numbering); Exodus 23:9 as ethical and narrative anchors
05.lore_reveal: Refusal of collective guilt produces a practical institution with real security costs
05.humour_target: Two displaced officials arguing over which of their abolished permits should admit the other

06.title: No Crown over the Refuge
06.want: Keep people fleeing conquest and civil war beyond rival rulers' possession
06.obstacle: Armed patrons promise defence in return for hostages and access to the refuge's residents
06.choice: Relocate the refuge through a costly route instead of accepting the protective bargain
06.consequence: Families evade conscription, but Lilith loses a defensible home and the political patronage that could rebuild it
source_passages: EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: relocation and Lilith's off-Garden polity
06.lore_reveal: A chosen limit can preserve agency while imposing a real strategic disadvantage
06.humour_target: Kings offering excellent protection against the problems their offers have just created

07.title: The Names Lilith Cannot Carry Alone
07.want: Preserve displaced people's identities without turning herself into their sole custodian
07.obstacle: Grief and fear make people offer her permanent control over their memories
07.choice: Train independent custodians and preserve each person's right to withhold testimony
07.consequence: Lilith relinquishes exclusive access while a dispersed memory network outlives the loss of any one sanctuary
source_passages: Lamentations; Psalms 137 as contextual testimony, not Lilith attestation
07.lore_reveal: Remembering can be shared without surrendering ownership of a lived experience
07.humour_target: An immortal finally admitting that being everybody's filing system is not a sustainable vocation

08.title: The Page They Call a Monster
08.want: Recover a damaged account of her actions without compelling universal admiration
08.obstacle: Custodians make access conditional on accepting the hostile identity their archive assigns her
08.choice: Preserve the hostile text as evidence while opening a separate channel for her own testimony
08.consequence: The archive keeps its history of vilification and gains a witness it can no longer describe only from outside
source_passages: Isaiah 34:14, translation and lilit identification disputed
Alphabet of Ben Sira: later reception must remain later
EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: encounter placed in transmission frame, not dated documentary claim
08.lore_reveal: A hostile received name can be historically real without accurately describing its target
08.humour_target: An archive requiring a visitor to confirm she is a monster before allowing her to correct the record

09.title: Lilith Does Not Speak for the Women
09.want: Keep endangered witnesses able to tell what they experienced after public violence
09.obstacle: Her older reputation and greater experience invite supporters to treat her as their authorized voice
09.choice: Provide shelter and routes while declining ownership of their testimony
09.consequence: The women retain independent accounts and the witness network gains protection without a replacement narrator
source_passages: Luke 8:1-3; Luke 24; John 20 as named women's source accounts
EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: Lilith's parallel protective activity, no Gospel attestation
09.lore_reveal: Shared experience of exclusion does not make Lilith identical to Mary, Eve, or every feminine witness
09.humour_target: Well-meaning organizers trying to solve silencing by selecting one exceptionally impressive spokeswoman

10.title: The Refuge Refuses a Creed Test
10.want: Keep distributed shelters usable by people with conflicting beliefs
10.obstacle: A growing institution offers resources in return for doctrinal control of admission
10.choice: Surrender the funding and distribute a leaner support network among independent houses
10.consequence: The network survives less comfortably and remains available to those the new institutional boundaries exclude
source_passages: Acts 6; 3 John; Hebrews 13 as hospitality counterpoints
EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: Lilith network and funding dispute
10.lore_reveal: A source's testimony cannot be inherited as ownership of everyone who needs shelter
10.humour_target: A doctrinal questionnaire attempting to establish whether hunger is sufficiently orthodox

11.title: Lilith Leaves Her Name with the Keepers
11.want: Make her history recoverable without making later readers recognize her on command
11.obstacle: Every archive has reasons to assimilate, erase, worship, or weaponize the name
11.choice: Leave corroborable fragments under separate custody and an explicit permission to question them
11.consequence: Modern remembering becomes possible through independent records rather than one overwhelming identity proclamation
source_passages: EDITORIAL-PROPOSAL: distributed evidence left by Lilith
11.lore_reveal: Later Lily's relation to Lilith remains a question with alternatives, not a title imposed by an archive
11.humour_target: A legendary figure negotiating to remain less certain than her publicity

12.title: Lily and Lilith Keep Two Places
12.POV: Lilith and Lily as distinct testimony positions
12.want: Understand their relation without sacrificing either person's lived history
12.obstacle: Reincarnation, fragment, vessel, and aspect models make incompatible claims about memory and agency
12.choice: Retain only the relation supported by shared evidence and reject the demand for total personal merger
12.consequence: Recovered identity enlarges relation while Lily's ordinary history and Lilith's long commitments remain separately accountable
12.lore_reveal: The staging is provisional and can use separate bodies, remembered dialogue, or parallel witnesses only after root resolves ontology; no simultaneous-body fact silently adopted
12.humour_target: An identity tribunal defeated by the practical requirement for two people to finish their own sentences

12.title: What Lilith and Eve Build Next
12.POV: Lilith and Eve, independently accountable collaborators
12.want: Keep a shared repair project viable without pretending their injuries or choices were equivalent
12.obstacle: Supporters demand either permanent enmity or a sentimental declaration that everything is forgiven
12.choice: Agree to a specific shared undertaking with limited access, separate claims, and room for actual companionship
12.consequence: A repaired refuge exists because the women cooperate; neither must surrender her account for their relationship to change
12.lore_reveal: Repair can precede, coexist with, or proceed without forgiveness; companionship is earned through conduct
12.humour_target: Two formidable women discovering that affection has not made either easier to share a workbench with
